law: Knowledge Once — domain substance is defined here once and projected to every artifact.

IDN.concepts: Identity is the constitutionally verifiable handle for any existence. It is namespace-partitioned, versioned, and lineage-carrying. External schemes (GTIN, EAN, UPC, ISBN, ISSN, IMEI, VIN, CUSIP, ISIN, HSN, SAC) and future schemes are represented WITHOUT schema change, as registry-driven fingerprints.
IDN.ontology: Identity ⊂ Existence. Identity has exactly one Namespace. Identity ≥ 1 Fingerprint. Identity has 0..n Aliases. Identity has 1 Lineage chain. Identity is referenced by every other primitive as its anchor.
IDN.taxonomy: By namespace: Platform / Tenant / External / Future. By strength: Provisional / Verified / Certified. By scope: Universal / Scoped / Ephemeral.
IDN.dataModel:
```yaml
Identity:
  identityId: <uuid v7, sort-friendly>
  namespace: <registry-driven, never hardcoded>
  version: <monotonic integer>
  lineage:
    parentId: <Identity|null>
    forkOf: <Identity|null>
  aliases: [<Alias>]
  fingerprints:
    - scheme: <registry scheme id>   # GTIN|EAN|VIN|...|future
      value: <normalized string>
      checksum: <registry-validated>
  signatures: [<Signature>]
  temporal: {validFrom, validTo, observedAt}
  metadata: {provenance, trustRef}
```
IDN.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Provisional
    Provisional --> Verified: evidence sufficient
    Verified --> Certified: authority attests
    Verified --> Deprecated: superseded
    Certified --> Deprecated: superseded
    Provisional --> Rejected: evidence refuted
    Deprecated --> [*]
```
workflow: resolve external scheme → registry lookup → fingerprint match → evidence capture → authority attestation → publish IdentityVerified
IDN.privacy: Aliases and fingerprints are pseudonymous. Direct identifiers require consent scope `identity:read`. Resolution logs are minimized and retention-governed by the Consent Architecture.
IDN.audit: Every resolution records: who resolved, which fingerprint matched, under which authority, with what evidence, at what confidence. Immutable, append-only, cryptographically chained.
IDN.twin: Identity Twin mirrors the real-world identifier state across registries (e.g., a GS1 GTIN changing ownership), continuously synchronized via the Twin Federation.
IDN.agent: Identity Agent monitors fingerprint collisions, lineage forks, and stale aliases, raising IdentityConflictDetected under governance.
IDN.runtime: Stateless resolution service with a versioned cache keyed by (namespace, normalized fingerprint). Cache invalidation on IdentityDeprecated/IdentityMerged events.
IDN.scaling: Read-heavy (>99%). Partition by namespace; replicate globally; resolve via content-addressable fingerprint index. Write path is authority-sharded.
IDN.multiTenant: Namespace isolation is mandatory: a tenant can never read another tenant's scoped identities unless an explicit cross-tenant Relationship + Policy permits it.
IDN.geo: Resolution is locally served per region with fingerprint-index replicas; authoritative write quorum remains in the tenant's home jurisdiction per Data Sovereignty.
IDN.failure: Fingerprint collision, alias loop, lineage cycle, authority unavailability, checksum drift on external scheme change.
IDN.recovery: Lineage is an immutable append-only log; recovery = replay. Deleted aliases are reconstructable from the chain. IdentityMerged is reversible via compensating event.
IDN.certification: Identity must pass checksum validity, lineage acyclicity, namespace ownership, and fingerprint uniqueness before it may anchor any Knowledge or Relationship.
IDN.migration: External scheme migration (e.g., UPC→GTIN-13) is a registry-driven re-fingerprint, never a schema migration. Old fingerprints remain valid aliases.
IDN.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant ID as Identity Domain
    participant EV as Evidence
    participant AU as Authority
    C->>ID: identity.resolve(fingerprint)
    ID->>EV: request attestation evidence
    EV-->>ID: evidence + confidence
    ID->>AU: request attestation
    AU-->>ID: attested
    ID-->>C: Identity (Verified)
```
IDN.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Resolving
    Resolving --> Matched: fingerprint hit
    Resolving --> Unmatched: no hit
    Matched --> Attesting
    Attesting --> Resolved
    Unmatched --> Provisional
```
IDN.blueprint: Build order for IDN: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by namespace: platform / tenant / external / future as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (identity.create, identity.resolve, identity.alias.add) and validate against IDN boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

KNW.concepts: Knowledge is validated understanding of reality — interpreted information with evidence and meaning. It is NOT data, NOT information, NOT evidence. It is derived from them. Every Knowledge element answers who asserted it, when, why, under which authority, based on what evidence, with what confidence.
KNW.ontology: Knowledge ⊂ Existence. Knowledge requires ≥1 Evidence. Knowledge has 1 Authority. Knowledge has Confidence ∈ [0,1]. Knowledge Types: Fact / Assertion / Hypothesis / Model / Belief / PolicyAsKnowledge / Regulation / Learned / Derived / Future.
KNW.taxonomy: By epistemic status: Proven / Supported / Contested / Refuted / Hypothetical. By source: Observed / Inferred / Asserted / Simulated. By volatility: Stable / Drifting / Volatile.
KNW.dataModel:
```yaml
Knowledge:
  knowledgeId: <Identity>
  type: <registry-driven type>
  assertion: <semantic statement>
  evidence: [<Evidence>]
  confidence: <0..1>
  provenance:
    assertedBy: <Authority>
    assertedAt: <Time>
    intent: <Intent>
  trust: <Trust>
  status: <Proven|Supported|Contested|Refuted|Hypothetical>
  supersededBy: <Knowledge|null>
```
KNW.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Asserted
    Asserted --> Supported: evidence corroborated
    Asserted --> Contested: contradiction detected
    Supported --> Proven: authority + evidence + high confidence
    Contested --> Refuted: evidence outweighs
    Contested --> Supported: contradiction resolved
    Proven --> Superseded: better knowledge
    Refuted --> [*]
    Superseded --> [*]
```
workflow: assert → evidence binding → trust computation → contradiction check → (contest | promote) → publish event
KNW.privacy: Assertions about persons require consent scope `knowledge:assert:pii`. Evidence retention follows the Consent Architecture; purge is a first-class command, not an afterthought.
KNW.audit: The seven explainability questions are mandatory fields. Knowledge chain is append-only; refutation never deletes — it supersedes, preserving history.
KNW.twin: Knowledge Twin tracks the real-world truth state of the subject (e.g., a regulation's enactment status) and flags drift between asserted and observed reality.
KNW.agent: Knowledge Agent continuously revalidates drifting knowledge, detects contradictions, and proposes supersessions under governance.
KNW.runtime: Write path is evidence-verified before commit; read path serves the current non-superseded head per query context.
KNW.scaling: Partition by subject Identity. Confidence computation is a read-side projection cached per (Knowledge, Context). Contradiction detection is a stream job.
KNW.multiTenant: Knowledge is tenant-scoped unless explicitly published to a shared ontology. Cross-tenant assertion requires a Relationship + Policy.
KNW.geo: Regulatory knowledge is jurisdiction-scoped; the same assertion may be Proven in one jurisdiction and Contested in another — both remain valid within Context.
KNW.failure: Evidence detachment, confidence drift beyond threshold, authority revocation mid-attestation, contradiction avalanche.
KNW.recovery: Never delete: supersede. Recovery = rebuild current-head projection from the append-only chain. Purge is governance-gated and leaves a tombstone.
KNW.certification: Knowledge must carry ≥1 evidence, an active authority, and a computed trust score above domain threshold to be read as Proven.
KNW.migration: Knowledge schema evolves by adding types to the registry; existing assertions are re-projected, never rewritten.
KNW.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Asserter
    participant KN as Knowledge Domain
    participant EV as Evidence
    participant TR as Trust
    A->>KN: knowledge.assert(statement, evidence)
    KN->>EV: verify evidence chain
    EV-->>KN: validity + provenance
    KN->>TR: compute trust
    TR-->>KN: score
    KN-->>A: KnowledgeAsserted
```
KNW.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Drafting
    Drafting --> Evidenced
    Evidenced --> Scored
    Scored --> Published
    Published --> Superseded
```
KNW.blueprint: Build order for KNW: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by epistemic status: proven / supported / contested / refuted / hypothetical as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (knowledge.assert, knowledge.contest, knowledge.supersede) and validate against KNW boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

REL.concepts: Relationship is a typed, contextualized, time-bounded connection between existences. Reality emerges through relationships, not through objects. Relationship ≠ Causality: a link is not a reason.
REL.ontology: Relationship has 1 source Identity, 1 target Identity, 1 RelationshipType (registry-driven), 0..n Context, temporal validity, and an Authority. Relationship types are open: Owns, Consumes, Produces, Requires, Provides, Contains, DependsOn, CompatibleWith, Replaces, Supersedes, Associates, Influences, Causes — plus unlimited future types from the registry.
REL.taxonomy: By direction: Directed / Undirected / Bidirectional. By strength: Structural / Behavioral / Ephemeral. By derivation: Declared / Inferred / Simulated.
REL.dataModel:
```yaml
Relationship:
  relationshipId: <Identity>
  relationshipType: <registry id>
  source: <Identity>
  target: <Identity>
  context: [<Context>]
  authority: <Authority>
  temporal: {validFrom, validTo}
  provenance: {declaredBy | inferredBy}
  trust: <Trust>
  metadata: <Metadata>
```
REL.graphModel: This IS the graph. (:Identity)-[:RELATIONSHIP_TYPE {context, temporal, trust}]->(:Identity). Traversal is context-filtered at query time.
REL.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Proposed
    Proposed --> Active: authority approves
    Active --> Weakened: trust decay
    Weakened --> Active: reinforced
    Active --> Expired: temporal end
    Active --> Retracted: governance
    Expired --> [*]
    Retracted --> [*]
```
workflow: validate endpoints exist → resolve type from registry → check authority → enforce context policy → commit → publish → integrity verify
authorities: Inference Authority (infers, lower trust by default)
REL.privacy: Relationships between persons are sensitive by default; traversal requires `relationship:read` scope plus a Context policy. Hidden-edge protection enforced.
REL.audit: Every traversal of a sensitive edge is logged with the seven explainability fields. Inferred relationships are always marked as such, never presented as declared.
REL.twin: Relationship Twin mirrors real-world connections (e.g., supplier links) and flags when observed reality diverges from declared relationships.
REL.agent: Relationship Agent discovers latent edges via the Inference Domain and proposes them with reduced trust pending corroboration.
REL.runtime: Graph-native store. Context filtering at traversal time — no pre-materialized per-context graphs, which would duplicate truth.
REL.scaling: Shard by source Identity hash. Multi-hop traversal is bounded by policy hop-limit. Hot vertices are cached as projections, never as truth.
REL.multiTenant: Cross-tenant edges require an explicit published RelationshipType + Policy. Default deny.
REL.geo: Edge locality follows Data Sovereignty: a vertex's authoritative edges live in its jurisdiction; replicas are read-only.
REL.failure: Dangling endpoint, type registry drift, temporal inversion (validFrom > validTo), orphaned inferred edges after retraction.
REL.recovery: Edges are immutable + temporal; recovery is replay. Retraction is a tombstone, not a delete. Integrity job rebuilds dangling detection.
REL.certification: Relationship must pass endpoint existence, type registry validity, authority jurisdiction, and temporal sanity.
REL.migration: New relationship types are registry additions — zero schema migration. Retired types become non-creatable but remain queryable historically.
REL.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant RL as Relationship Domain
    participant RG as Registry
    participant AU as Authority
    C->>RL: create(source, target, type)
    RL->>RG: resolve relationship type
    RG-->>RL: type definition
    RL->>AU: authorize over source
    AU-->>RL: approved
    RL-->>C: RelationshipCreated
```
REL.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Validating
    Validating --> Authorized
    Authorized --> Committed
    Committed --> Verified
```
REL.blueprint: Build order for REL: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by direction: directed / undirected / bidirectional as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (relationship.create, relationship.retype, relationship.expire) and validate against REL boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

CTX.concepts: Context is the applicability boundary that changes how reality is projected. Context ≠ Perspective: a context is a scope; a perspective is an observer's interpretation. The same primitives project differently per context.
CTX.ontology: Context is hierarchical and compositional. Context types are registry-driven: Geographical, Organizational, Commercial, Customer, Contractual, Marketplace, Legal, Regulatory, Operational, Behavioral, Temporal, Digital, Physical, Future. A context constrains which Policies and Authorities are in force.
CTX.taxonomy: By breadth: Universal / Regional / Local / Instance. By nature: Structural (geo, org) / Temporal (time window) / Situational (session, intent).
CTX.dataModel:
```yaml
Context:
  contextId: <Identity>
  contextType: <registry id>
  hierarchy:
    parentId: <Context|null>
  constraints: [<constraint expressions>]
  policies: [<Policy>]
  authorities: [<Authority>]
  temporal: {effectiveFrom, effectiveTo}
  metadata: <Metadata>
```
CTX.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Defined
    Defined --> Active: effectiveFrom reached
    Active --> Suspended: governance hold
    Suspended --> Active: released
    Active --> Expired: effectiveTo reached
    Expired --> [*]
```
workflow: define → attach policies → resolve hierarchy → detect overlap conflicts → activate → publish effective policy set
authorities: Jurisdiction Authority (creates contexts in its scope)
CTX.privacy: Context may implicitly narrow data access; privacy impact is asserted on creation and re-audited on policy attachment.
CTX.audit: Context resolution is logged: which contexts applied, in what precedence, and which policy won on conflict. Precedence is deterministic, never incidental.
CTX.twin: Context Twin mirrors real-world scope changes (e.g., a new regulatory regime activating) and projects the change through affected artifacts.
CTX.agent: Context Agent detects overlapping contexts with contradictory policies and escalates per the Contradiction Architecture.
CTX.runtime: Resolution is a memoized hierarchy walk. Effective policy set = union of ancestor policies with deterministic conflict precedence (child > parent; specific > general).
CTX.scaling: Hierarchy is shallow and cache-friendly; resolution results cached per (Identity, Context) with invalidation on ContextPolicyAttached.
CTX.multiTenant: A tenant's contexts are isolated. Cross-context projection requires explicit delegation.
CTX.geo: Geographical contexts are the primary sovereignty mechanism — data residency policy attaches here, not in application code.
CTX.failure: Cycle in hierarchy, contradictory policies at same precedence, orphaned policy attachment, temporal overlap ambiguity.
CTX.recovery: Contexts are immutable versions; recovery = repoint to prior version. Policy attachments are event-sourced and reversible.
CTX.certification: Context must pass acyclicity, jurisdiction ownership, policy compatibility, and deterministic precedence before activation.
CTX.migration: New context types are registry additions. Existing contexts re-project on type definition change.
CTX.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant CT as Context Domain
    participant PL as Policy
    C->>CT: resolve(identity)
    CT->>CT: walk hierarchy
    CT->>PL: gather effective policies
    PL-->>CT: policy set
    CT-->>C: resolved context
```
CTX.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Defining
    Defining --> Attached
    Attached --> Resolved
    Resolved --> Active
```
CTX.blueprint: Build order for CTX: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by breadth: universal / regional / local / instance as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (context.create, context.attachPolicy, context.delegate) and validate against CTX boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

POL.concepts: Policy is behavioral governance — the statement of what must, may, or must not happen. Policy ≠ Rule: policy is intent; the rule is its executable projection. All behavior derives from policy. Nothing executes that policy does not permit.
POL.ontology: Policy has Conditions, Actions, Priorities, Exceptions, and an Authority. Policy is resolved within a Context. Policy projects into Rules. Policy never executes directly — that is the Rule Domain's role.
POL.taxonomy: By force: Mandatory / Permissive / Prohibitive. By scope: Universal / Jurisdictional / Contextual / Instance. By origin: Constitutional / Regulatory / Organizational / Learned.
POL.dataModel:
```yaml
Policy:
  policyId: <Identity>
  intent: <Intent>
  conditions: [<registry expression>]
  actions: [<registry action>]
  priorities: [<int>]
  exceptions: [<Policy exception>]
  authority: <Authority>
  context: [<Context>]
  temporal: {effectiveFrom, effectiveTo}
  status: <Draft|Active|Retired>
```
POL.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft
    Draft --> Validated
    Validated --> Active
    Active --> Conflict
    Conflict --> Active: resolved
    Active --> Retired
    Retired --> [*]
```
workflow: author intent → validate against constitution → detect conflicts → project to Rules → activate → publish → re-project on change
POL.privacy: Policies governing personal data must reference a lawful basis via the Consent Architecture; purpose limitation is a first-class condition.
POL.audit: Every PolicyEvaluated records the input facts, matched conditions, chosen action, and precedence rationale. Denials carry appeal references.
POL.twin: Policy Twin mirrors real-world regulatory text and flags when observed regulation drifts from enacted policy.
POL.agent: Policy Agent detects conflicts between overlapping policies and proposes precedence resolutions under governance.
POL.runtime: Evaluation is a forward-chaining pass over the effective policy set for a Context; result is cached per (subject, context, fact-hash).
POL.scaling: Policy resolution is read-heavy and cacheable; invalidation is event-driven on PolicyActivated/PolicyRetired in the affected Context.
POL.multiTenant: Tenant policies cannot override constitutional policy; precedence is Constitutional > Jurisdictional > Tenant > Contextual.
POL.geo: Jurisdictional policy is geo-scoped; where two jurisdictions conflict, Data Sovereignty policy decides the applicable set — both are recorded, neither is silently dropped.
POL.failure: Conflict at equal precedence, unsatisfiable condition set, projection failure to Rules, policy storm (mass activation).
POL.recovery: Policies are versioned and event-sourced; retirement is reversible. Projection failures roll back to the last validated projection.
POL.certification: Policy must pass constitutional conformance, conflict precedence determinism, and successful rule projection before activation.
POL.migration: Policy language evolves by registry expression extension — never by changing the policy schema.
POL.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant PL as Policy Domain
    participant RU as Rule Domain
    C->>PL: policy.create(intent)
    PL->>PL: validate constitutionality
    PL->>RU: project to executable rules
    RU-->>PL: rules projected
    PL-->>C: PolicyActivated
```
POL.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Authored
    Authored --> Validated
    Validated --> Projected
    Projected --> Active
    Active --> Retired
```
POL.blueprint: Build order for POL: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by force: mandatory / permissive / prohibitive as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (policy.create, policy.activate, policy.retire) and validate against POL boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

RUL.concepts: Rule is the executable constraint derived from Policy. Rule ≠ Policy and Rule ≠ Decision. Rules are the machine-runnable projection of governance intent. A rule never contradicts its parent policy.
RUL.ontology: Rule has exactly 1 parent Policy, an executable expression, an evaluation order, and an effect. Rules are composable but never self-referential.
RUL.taxonomy: By effect: Permit / Deny / Require / Transform / Notify / Defer. By evaluation: Boolean / Threshold / Set-membership / Registry-lookup / Composite.
RUL.dataModel:
```yaml
Rule:
  ruleId: <Identity>
  derivedFrom: <Policy>
  expression: <registry expression id>
  effect: <Permit|Deny|Require|Transform|Notify|Defer>
  priority: <int>
  evalOrder: <int>
  onConflict: <registry strategy>
  temporal: {effectiveFrom, effectiveTo}
```
RUL.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Projected
    Projected --> Validated
    Validated --> Enabled
    Enabled --> Disabled
    Disabled --> Enabled
    Enabled --> [*]
```
workflow: policy projects rule → static validation → conflict reconciliation → enable → evaluate at runtime
authorities: Inherits parent policy's authority; no independent authority.
RUL.privacy: Rule expressions over personal data must carry the consent scope of their parent policy; evaluation logs minimize captured facts.
RUL.audit: Every RuleEvaluated records input facts, matched rule, effect, and evaluation time. Deterministic replay must reproduce identical outcomes.
RUL.twin: Rule Twin tracks real-world enforcement outcomes and flags divergence between rule effect and observed behavior.
RUL.agent: Rule Agent detects unreachable or redundant rules and proposes pruning under governance.
RUL.runtime: Rules compile to a decision DAG per Context; evaluation is fact-driven with short-circuit on Deny for mandatory policies.
RUL.scaling: DAG compilation cached per policy version; runtime evaluation is sub-millisecond. Hot paths are precompiled.
RUL.multiTenant: Rules are tenant-scoped through their parent policy; cross-tenant evaluation is constitutionally forbidden.
RUL.geo: Rule evaluation is local per region; the compiled DAG is replicated, authoritative projection stays in jurisdiction.
RUL.failure: Non-deterministic expression, projection drift from policy, evaluation timeout, conflicting effects at equal priority.
RUL.recovery: Rules are derived, so recovery is re-projection from the parent policy. No rule is ever hand-restored.
RUL.certification: Rule must pass determinism (same facts → same effect), policy conformance, and termination guarantees.
RUL.migration: Expression language evolves by registry; existing rules re-project on language version change.
RUL.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant RT as Runtime
    participant RU as Rule Domain
    participant PL as Policy
    RT->>RU: evaluate(facts, context)
    RU->>RU: load compiled DAG
    RU->>RU: evaluate rules
    RU-->>RT: effect
    RU->>PL: report evaluation
```
RUL.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Loading
    Loading --> Evaluating
    Evaluating --> Effect
    Effect --> Logging
```
RUL.blueprint: Build order for RUL: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by effect: permit / deny / require / transform / notify / defer as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (rule.evaluate, rule.validate, rule.reorder) and validate against RUL boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

AUT.concepts: Authority is the right to govern within a jurisdiction. Authority ≠ Ownership: authority is the right; ownership is the responsibility. Authority is delegable, revocable, and always bounded.
AUT.ontology: Authority has a Jurisdiction, Rights, Responsibilities, and a delegating parent Authority. Types: Platform / Tenant / Country / Regulatory / Corporate / Future — all registry-driven.
AUT.taxonomy: By scope: Universal / Jurisdictional / Organizational / Contextual. By source: Constitutional / Delegated / Assumed (weakest) / Attested.
AUT.dataModel:
```yaml
Authority:
  authorityId: <Identity>
  type: <registry id>
  jurisdiction: <Context>
  rights: [<registry capability>]
  responsibilities: [<registry obligation>]
  delegatedFrom: <Authority|null>
  temporal: {grantedAt, revokedAt}
  status: <Active|Revoked|Expired>
```
AUT.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Granted
    Granted --> Delegated
    Delegated --> Challenged
    Challenged --> Active: upheld
    Challenged --> Revoked: upheld challenge
    Granted --> Revoked
    Revoked --> [*]
```
workflow: grant → scope to jurisdiction → delegate with reduced rights → challenge on suspicion → revoke with cascade to derived authorities
authorities: Constitutional Authority is self-sovereign; all others derive from it.
permissions: authority.grant (holder of the right being granted)
AUT.privacy: Authority chains over personal jurisdictions are auditable but access-restricted; revocation of consent cascades to derived grants.
AUT.audit: Every governed action records its full authority chain back to the Constitutional Authority. Untraceable chains are denied by default.
AUT.twin: Authority Twin mirrors real-world governance changes (e.g., regulatory body restructure) and cascades them through delegations.
AUT.agent: Authority Agent detects over-broad delegations and authority chain anomalies, challenging them under governance.
AUT.runtime: Resolution walks the delegation chain with memoization; revocation invalidates the entire derived subtree.
AUT.scaling: Chain depth is bounded by constitution. Resolution cached per (Authority, right); invalidation on AuthorityRevoked.
AUT.multiTenant: Tenant authority is bounded by constitutional authority — delegation cannot exceed the granter's rights (monotone decreasing).
AUT.geo: Jurisdictional authority is geo-scoped; cross-jurisdiction action requires authority recognized in both — or is denied.
AUT.failure: Delegation cycle, rights inflation (child > parent), orphaned chain after revocation, jurisdiction gap.
AUT.recovery: Chains are append-only; revocation is a terminal event. Recovery rebuilds the effective-authority projection from the chain.
AUT.certification: Authority must pass chain traceability, rights monotonicity, jurisdiction validity, and non-expiration.
AUT.migration: New authority types are registry additions; existing chains re-resolve on type change.
AUT.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Actor
    participant AU as Authority Domain
    participant CT as Context
    A->>AU: resolve(authority, right)
    AU->>AU: walk delegation chain
    AU->>CT: confirm jurisdiction
    CT-->>AU: in jurisdiction
    AU-->>A: decision
```
AUT.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Resolving
    Resolving --> Tracing
    Tracing --> Scoping
    Scoping --> Decided
```
AUT.blueprint: Build order for AUT: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by scope: universal / jurisdictional / organizational / contextual as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (authority.grant, authority.delegate, authority.revoke) and validate against AUT boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

TRS.concepts: Trust is computed confidence in an assertion, derived from evidence. Trust ≠ Evidence and Trust ≠ Faith: it is a score, recomputable, always current, never asserted. Trust degrades without corroboration.
TRS.ontology: Trust is a function over (Evidence, Authority, Consistency, Provenance, Confidence). Trust has a timestamp — stale trust decays. Trust is per-Context.
TRS.taxonomy: By subject: Identity / Knowledge / Relationship / Authority / Agent. By method: Evidence-weighted / Authority-weighted / Consistency-weighted / Consensus / Decay-based.
TRS.dataModel:
```yaml
Trust:
  trustId: <Identity>
  subject: <Identity>
  evidenceScore: <0..1>
  authorityScore: <0..1>
  consistencyScore: <0..1>
  provenanceScore: <0..1>
  confidenceScore: <0..1>
  composite: <0..1, registry formula>
  computedAt: <Time>
  context: <Context>
  decayPolicy: <Policy>
```
TRS.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Stale
    Stale --> Computing
    Computing --> Current
    Current --> Stale: decay interval
    Current --> Disputed
    Disputed --> Computing
```
workflow: gather evidence → weight by authority → measure consistency → score provenance → apply confidence → composite → publish → schedule decay
authorities: Trust Domain computes; it does not assert. Authority Domain supplies the authority weight; Trust never overrides it.
TRS.privacy: Trust over personal subjects is derived from minimized evidence; raw evidence is not exposed, only the score and its factor breakdown.
TRS.audit: Every score is reproducible: inputs, weights, formula version, and timestamp are recorded. A score that cannot be reproduced is void.
TRS.twin: Trust Twin tracks real-world reputation drift and flags divergence between computed trust and observed outcomes.
TRS.agent: Trust Agent continuously recomputes decaying scores and raises TrustThresholdCrossed for governance attention.
TRS.runtime: Scores are read-optimized projections recomputed on evidence change or decay tick; never stored as primary truth.
TRS.scaling: Recomputation is a stream job over evidence events; composite scores cached per (subject, context) with decay-aware TTL.
TRS.multiTenant: Trust is tenant-scoped; a subject's trust in one tenant says nothing about another unless a shared Context exists.
TRS.geo: Trust factors are jurisdiction-weighted: an authority's weight is Context-dependent, so the same evidence yields different scores per jurisdiction — by design.
TRS.failure: Evidence starvation, formula drift across versions, authority score corruption, decay cascade.
TRS.recovery: Scores are recomputable from evidence history; a corrupted score is regenerated, never restored from backup.
TRS.certification: Trust score must be reproducible, timestamped, formula-versioned, and within threshold for its subject's certifications.
TRS.migration: Formula evolves by registry version; recomputation triggers on version change with full history replay.
TRS.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant E as Evidence Event
    participant TR as Trust Domain
    participant AU as Authority
    E->>TR: new evidence
    TR->>AU: authority weight
    AU-->>TR: weight
    TR->>TR: compute composite
    TR-->>E: TrustComputed
```
TRS.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Evidenced
    Evidenced --> Weighted
    Weighted --> Composed
    Composed --> Published
```
TRS.blueprint: Build order for TRS: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by subject: identity / knowledge / relationship / authority / agent as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (trust.recompute, trust.decay, trust.cite) and validate against TRS boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

EVD.concepts: Evidence is proof supporting an assertion. Evidence ≠ Knowledge and Evidence ≠ Trust: it supports knowledge and feeds trust; it is not itself understanding. Nothing exists without evidence.
EVD.ontology: Evidence has a Source, a Proof payload, Validity, and Confidence. Evidence types: Document / Signature / Timestamp / Attestation / Observation / Receipt / Hash-witness / Future type — all registry-driven.
EVD.taxonomy: By strength: Cryptographic / Attested / Observed / Claimed (weakest). By permanence: Immutable / Temporal / Revocable.
EVD.dataModel:
```yaml
Evidence:
  evidenceId: <Identity>
  type: <registry id>
  source: <Identity|Authority>
  proof: <content-addressed payload reference>
  validity: {verifiedAt, method, expiresAt}
  confidence: <0..1>
  chain: [parent evidence]
  metadata: <Metadata>
```
EVD.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Submitted
    Submitted --> Verified: method passes
    Submitted --> Rejected: method fails
    Verified --> Revoked: authority revokes
    Verified --> Expired: temporal end
    Revoked --> [*]
    Expired --> [*]
```
workflow: submit → select verification method from registry → verify → chain to parent evidence → publish → schedule expiry
EVD.privacy: Proof payloads are content-addressed and access-scoped; personal evidence follows the Consent Architecture's retention and erasure policy.
EVD.audit: Every verification records method, verifier, timestamp, and result. Revocation never deletes — it invalidates downstream support and is logged.
EVD.twin: Evidence Twin mirrors real-world proof status (e.g., a license expiring) and propagates expiry to dependent Knowledge.
EVD.agent: Evidence Agent detects expiring and weak-chain evidence, triggering re-verification before downstream trust degrades.
EVD.runtime: Verification is method-dispatched from the registry; hot path caches verification results keyed by content hash.
EVD.scaling: Payloads are stored once, content-addressed; verification results are cached and invalidated on EvidenceRevoked.
EVD.multiTenant: Evidence is tenant-scoped; cross-tenant citation requires explicit published relationship.
EVD.geo: Proof payloads follow Data Sovereignty residency; verification method availability varies by jurisdiction (e.g., eIDAS vs. eID).
EVD.failure: Method unavailability, chain breakage, hash collision (mitigated by algorithm agility), revocation storm.
EVD.recovery: Content-addressed storage is self-verifying; recovery re-verifies hashes. Revoked evidence stays invalid — integrity over recoverability.
EVD.certification: Evidence must pass method verification, chain integrity, non-expiration, and source authority validity.
EVD.migration: New verification methods are registry additions; existing evidence re-verifies on method activation.
EVD.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Submitter
    participant EV as Evidence Domain
    participant VA as Verification Authority
    S->>EV: submit(proof, type)
    EV->>EV: resolve method
    EV->>VA: verify
    VA-->>EV: verified
    EV-->>S: EvidenceVerified
```
EVD.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Received
    Received --> MethodResolved
    MethodResolved --> Verified
    Verified --> Chained
```
EVD.blueprint: Build order for EVD: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by strength: cryptographic / attested / observed / claimed (weakest) as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (evidence.submit, evidence.verify, evidence.revoke) and validate against EVD boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

OBS.concepts: Observation is captured reality at a point in time. Observation ≠ Inference: it is what was sensed, never what was derived. Observations are the raw feed from which Knowledge, Trust, and Twins derive.
OBS.ontology: Observation has a Source, a captured Payload, a Timestamp, and a Context. Sources: Transactions, Logs, Events, Documents, Images, Video, Voice, IoT, External APIs, Human Inputs, Agent Inputs — all registry-driven and extensible.
OBS.taxonomy: By source: Machine / Human / Agent / External. By nature: Discrete / Continuous / Composite. By fidelity: Raw / Normalized / Enriched.
OBS.dataModel:
```yaml
Observation:
  observationId: <Identity>
  source: <Identity>
  sourceType: <registry id>
  capturedAt: <Time>
  context: <Context>
  payload: <content-addressed>
  fidelity: <Raw|Normalized|Enriched>
  metadata: <Metadata>
```
OBS.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Ingested
    Ingested --> Validated
    Validated --> Normalized
    Normalized --> Enriched
    Validated --> Quarantined
    Quarantined --> Normalized: remediated
```
workflow: ingest → schema-validate against source type → normalize → enrich with context → publish to stream → persist content-addressed
OBS.privacy: Observations of persons are privacy-sensitive by default; enrichment of personal data requires consent scope and purpose limitation.
OBS.audit: Every ingest records source, timestamp, context, and validation outcome. Quarantine reasons are mandatory and reviewable.
OBS.twin: Observation is the primary synchronization feed into Digital Twins — the 'reality' side of the twin loop.
OBS.agent: Observation Agent detects anomalies, drift, and source degradation, quarantining suspicious feeds under governance.
OBS.runtime: Ingest is a high-throughput append-only stream; enrichment is a pipeline stage; replay is first-class for recovery.
OBS.scaling: Partition by source and time bucket; retention is policy-driven per source type; cold storage is registry-configured.
OBS.multiTenant: Observations are tenant-scoped at ingest; a source cannot write into another tenant's stream.
OBS.geo: Ingest endpoints are region-local for latency; residency follows the source's Context, enforced at write time.
OBS.failure: Schema violation, source spoofing, backpressure overload, clock skew, duplicate ingest.
OBS.recovery: Idempotent ingest via source-assigned sequence numbers; replay rebuilds downstream projections exactly.
OBS.certification: Observation must pass source authorization, schema validity, timestamp sanity, and context binding.
OBS.migration: New source types are registry additions; the ingest pipeline dispatches by type without code change.
OBS.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Source
    participant OB as Observation Domain
    participant ST as Stream
    S->>OB: ingest(payload)
    OB->>OB: validate + normalize
    OB->>ST: publish
    ST-->>OB: ack
    OB-->>S: ObservationIngested
```
OBS.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Receiving
    Receiving --> Validating
    Validating --> Normalizing
    Normalizing --> Streaming
```
OBS.blueprint: Build order for OBS: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by source: machine / human / agent / external as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (observation.ingest, observation.normalize, observation.enrich) and validate against OBS boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

INF.concepts: Inference is derived reality — discovery without explicit definition. Inference ≠ Observation: it is what was concluded, not what was sensed. Inferences carry lower trust by default and are always labeled as derived.
INF.ontology: Inference has a Method, input Observations/Knowledge, a derived output, and a Confidence. Methods: Statistical / Graph / Semantic / Causal / Neural / Hybrid — registry-driven.
INF.taxonomy: By output: New Relationship / New Knowledge / New Risk / New Capability / New Pattern. By method: Deductive-projected / Inductive / Abductive / Analogical.
INF.dataModel:
```yaml
Inference:
  inferenceId: <Identity>
  method: <registry id>
  inputs: [<Observation|Knowledge>]
  output: <Relationship|Knowledge|Risk|Pattern>
  confidence: <0..1>
  trust: <Trust, reduced by default>
  context: <Context>
  reproducible: <bool>
```
INF.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Candidate
    Candidate --> Promoted: corroboration
    Candidate --> Rejected: refuted
    Promoted --> Demoted: trust decay
    Rejected --> [*]
```
workflow: select method → gather inputs within consent scope → run → assign reduced trust → present as candidate → promote on corroboration
authorities: Promotion Authority (domain authority in output scope)
INF.privacy: Inferences about persons are sensitive; no inference over personal data without consent scope covering the method's purpose.
INF.audit: Every inference records method, inputs, confidence, and is reproducible or void. Inferences are never presented as observations.
INF.twin: Inference feeds Twins with predicted states, clearly separated from observed twin state.
INF.agent: Inference Agent is the primary autonomous discovery mechanism, governed by Agent Safety and the constitution.
INF.runtime: Methods are registry-dispatched plugins running in a sandbox with resource limits; outputs never mutate reality directly.
INF.scaling: Inference is a batch/stream job; candidates queue for promotion; hot methods are pre-warmed.
INF.multiTenant: Inferences never cross tenant boundaries; cross-tenant inference requires published relationship and policy.
INF.geo: Inference over regulated data runs in-jurisdiction; method availability respects local regulation.
INF.failure: Method drift, input starvation, unreproducible output, confidence inflation.
INF.recovery: Inferences are re-derivable; promotion is reversible to candidate. Unreproducible inferences are auto-rejected.
INF.certification: Inference must be reproducible, method-registered, consent-scoped, and below promotion threshold until corroborated.
INF.migration: New methods are registry additions; rerun on method version change.
INF.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant I as Inference Domain
    participant M as Method (registry)
    participant TR as Trust
    I->>M: run(inputs)
    M-->>I: derived output
    I->>TR: assign reduced trust
    TR-->>I: score
    I-->>I: InferenceProduced (candidate)
```
INF.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Selecting
    Selecting --> Running
    Running --> Scoring
    Scoring --> Candidate
```
INF.blueprint: Build order for INF: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by output: new relationship / new knowledge / new risk / new capability / new pattern as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (inference.run, inference.promote, inference.reject) and validate against INF boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

RSN.concepts: Reasoning is the deliberate derivation of conclusions under governance. Reasoning ≠ Inference: reasoning is explainable, step-wise, and auditable; inference may be statistical and opaque. Every reasoning chain is reconstructable.
RSN.ontology: Reasoning has a Mode (Deductive / Inductive / Abductive / Constraint / Policy / Semantic / Causal), a chain of steps, premises, and a conclusion. Each step is itself recorded.
RSN.taxonomy: By mode: Deductive / Inductive / Abductive / Constraint-satisfaction / Policy-based / Semantic / Causal. By purpose: Explanation / Prediction / Diagnosis / Planning / Justification.
RSN.dataModel:
```yaml
Reasoning:
  reasoningId: <Identity>
  mode: <registry id>
  premises: [<Knowledge|Observation>]
  steps:
    - stepNo: <int>
      rule: <Rule|registry inference rule>
      input: <facts>
      output: <fact>
  conclusion: <Knowledge|Decision>
  explainable: true   # mandatory
  context: <Context>
```
RSN.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Premised
    Premised --> Stepping
    Stepping --> Concluded
    Concluded --> Validated
    Validated --> Published
```
workflow: load premises within scope → apply mode → record each step → conclude → validate chain → publish with explanation
authorities: Reasoning Authority (runs modes); conclusion authority follows the Knowledge/Decision domain rules.
RSN.privacy: Premises containing personal data require consent scope; explanations minimize exposed facts while remaining reconstructable.
RSN.audit: The chain is the audit. A conclusion without a reconstructable chain is constitutionally void.
RSN.twin: Reasoning produces explanations for twin state divergence — why the twin differs from observed reality.
RSN.agent: Reasoning Agent is the explainable counterpart to the Inference Agent, justifying autonomous conclusions.
RSN.runtime: Step-wise execution with checkpointing; long chains are resumable. Every step is persisted before the next runs.
RSN.scaling: Chains are partitioned by conclusion subject; step storage is append-only and deduplicated by hash.
RSN.multiTenant: Reasoning never mixes premises across tenants.
RSN.geo: Reasoning over jurisdiction-scoped knowledge stays in jurisdiction.
RSN.failure: Step invalidation, premise revocation mid-chain, mode unavailability, unbounded chain length.
RSN.recovery: Chains are replayable; a revoked premise invalidates downstream steps deterministically and re-triggers reasoning.
RSN.certification: Reasoning must be fully reconstructable, mode-registered, scope-valid, and step-auditable.
RSN.migration: New modes are registry additions; existing chains preserve their mode version.
RSN.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Reasoner
    participant RS as Reasoning Domain
    participant KN as Knowledge
    R->>RS: run(mode, premises)
    RS->>RS: step, persist, step
    RS->>KN: conclude
    KN-->>RS: KnowledgeAsserted
    RS-->>R: ReasoningCompleted + chain
```
RSN.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Loading
    Loading --> Stepping
    Stepping --> Concluding
    Concluding --> Explaining
```
RSN.blueprint: Build order for RSN: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by mode: deductive / inductive / abductive / constraint-satisfaction / policy-based / semantic / causal as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (reasoning.run, reasoning.explain, reasoning.validate) and validate against RSN boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

SIM.concepts: Simulation is possible reality. Simulation ≠ Reality: it never mutates actual reality, never approves policy, and never spends money. Simulations are throwaway, reproducible, and clearly labeled.
SIM.ontology: Simulation has a Model, input State, perturbations, and output Possibilities. Types: Pricing / Risk / Compliance / Expansion / Operational / Future Scenario / Economic — registry-driven.
SIM.taxonomy: By horizon: Now / Near / Far. By fidelity: Order-of-magnitude / Approximate / High-fidelity. By purpose: Decision-support / Stress-test / Exploration.
SIM.dataModel:
```yaml
Simulation:
  simulationId: <Identity>
  modelType: <registry id>
  inputState: <snapshot reference>
  perturbations: [<registry perturbation>]
  outputs: [Possibility]
  runs: <int>
  reproducible: <bool>
  temporal: {simulatedFrom, simulatedTo}
```
SIM.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Queued
    Queued --> Running
    Running --> Completed
    Running --> Failed
    Running --> Cancelled
    Completed --> Archived
```
workflow: snapshot input state → select model → apply perturbations under budget → yield possibilities → label as simulated → archive
authorities: Simulation Authority (runs models); no authority to mutate reality — separation is constitutional.
SIM.privacy: Simulations over personal populations use synthetic or aggregated inputs; no individual-level personal simulation without consent.
SIM.audit: Every run records model version, inputs, perturbations, and resource cost. Outputs are watermarked as simulated in every projection.
SIM.twin: Twins provide the initial state for simulations; simulations never write back to twins — one-directional by law.
SIM.agent: Simulation Agent pre-runs scenarios for autonomous planning, governed by Agent Safety budgets.
SIM.runtime: Runs in an isolated sandbox with compute/time budget enforcement; outputs are content-addressed and immutable.
SIM.scaling: Embarrassingly parallel across perturbation grids; results cache by (model, input-hash, perturbation-hash).
SIM.multiTenant: Simulations never mix tenant states; cross-tenant scenarios require published relationship.
SIM.geo: Heavy compute runs in the tenant's authorized regions; regulated data never leaves jurisdiction for simulation.
SIM.failure: Model divergence, budget exhaustion, non-convergence, input state staleness.
SIM.recovery: Simulations are disposable; recovery is re-run. Archived results are content-addressed and self-verifying.
SIM.certification: Simulation must be reproducible, budget-bounded, reality-isolated, and clearly labeled in all outputs.
SIM.migration: New model types are registry additions; archived runs preserve their model version.
SIM.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant SI as Simulation Domain
    participant TW as Twin Federation
    C->>SI: run(model, perturbations)
    SI->>TW: snapshot current state
    TW-->>SI: state
    SI->>SI: run under budget
    SI-->>C: Possibilities (simulated)
```
SIM.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Snapshotting
    Snapshotting --> Modeling
    Modeling --> Yielding
    Yielding --> Archiving
```
SIM.blueprint: Build order for SIM: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by horizon: now / near / far as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (simulation.run, simulation.cancel, simulation.compare) and validate against SIM boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

CAU.concepts: Causality is the reason one existence influences another. Causality ≠ Relationship: a link says 'connected'; causality says 'because'. Causal claims require intervention-grade evidence, not correlation.
CAU.ontology: Causality has a Cause, an Effect, a Mechanism, and an Evidence grade. Claims are typed: Direct / Mediated / Contributory / Counterfactual.
CAU.taxonomy: By strength: Proven (interventional) / Supported (observational + mechanism) / Hypothesized (correlational) / Refuted.
CAU.dataModel:
```yaml
Causality:
  causalityId: <Identity>
  cause: <Identity|Event>
  effect: <Identity|Event>
  mechanism: <registry id>
  evidenceGrade: <Proven|Supported|Hypothesized|Refuted>
  evidence: [<Evidence>]
  confounders: [<Identity>]
  context: <Context>
  trust: <Trust>
```
CAU.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Hypothesized
    Hypothesized --> Supported: mechanism + obs evidence
    Supported --> Proven: interventional evidence
    Hypothesized --> Refuted
    Supported --> Refuted
    Proven --> Refined
```
workflow: observe correlation → propose mechanism → rule out confounders → upgrade on interventional evidence → publish grade
authorities: Causality Authority (asserts under evidence standards); interventional claims require elevated authority.
CAU.privacy: Causal claims over persons require aggregated or consented evidence; individual-level causal claims are prohibited without consent.
CAU.audit: Every claim records evidence grade, confounders considered, and method. Correlational claims are never projected as causal.
CAU.twin: Causal models explain twin divergence and predict intervention outcomes on twins before reality is touched.
CAU.agent: Causality Agent continuously downgrades unsupported claims and flags spurious correlations for review.
CAU.runtime: Graph traversal for impact analysis; confounder sets computed at assert time and rechecked on related Knowledge change.
CAU.scaling: Causal graphs are partitioned by subject; impact queries are bounded by policy depth.
CAU.multiTenant: Causal claims never cross tenant boundaries without published relationship.
CAU.geo: Evidence standards are jurisdiction-aware; a claim Proven under one regime may be Supported elsewhere — both recorded.
CAU.failure: Confounder omission, grade inflation, mechanism invalidation, cyclic causal claims.
CAU.recovery: Claims are versioned; refutation supersedes rather than deletes, preserving the history of what was believed and why.
CAU.certification: Claim must pass mechanism validity, confounder enumeration, evidence-grade honesty, and acyclicity.
CAU.migration: New mechanisms are registry additions; existing claims re-grade on mechanism version change.
CAU.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Asserter
    participant CA as Causality Domain
    participant EV as Evidence
    A->>CA: assert(cause, effect, mechanism)
    CA->>EV: gather + grade evidence
    EV-->>CA: grade
    CA->>CA: enumerate confounders
    CA-->>A: CausalityAsserted
```
CAU.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Correlating
    Correlating --> Mechanizing
    Mechanizing --> Confounding
    Confounding --> Grading
```
CAU.blueprint: Build order for CAU: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by strength: proven (interventional) / supported (observational + mechanism) / hypothesized (correlational) / refuted as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (causality.assert, causality.refine, causality.refute) and validate against CAU boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

EVO.concepts: Evolution is governed change over time that preserves history. Nothing evolves without governance; nothing that evolved is forgotten. Evolution covers Ontology, Schema, Policy, Capability, Workflow, API, Agent, and Knowledge evolution.
EVO.ontology: Evolution has a Subject, a Change, a Rationale, an Authority, and a preserved History. Emergence is evolution's un-planned cousin: properties arising from interaction that were not present in the parts.
EVO.taxonomy: By intent: Planned / Emergent. By impact: Additive / Breaking / Deprecated-path. By scope: Primitive-level (constitution only) / Registry-level / Projection-level.
EVO.dataModel:
```yaml
Evolution:
  evolutionId: <Identity>
  subject: <Identity>
  changeType: <registry id>
  from: <prior version ref>
  to: <new version ref>
  rationale: <Knowledge>
  authority: <Authority>
  temporal: {effectiveAt}
  supersession: {priorVersions: [...], historyPreserved: true}
```
EVO.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Proposed
    Proposed --> Approved
    Approved --> Activated
    Activated --> RolledBack
    Activated --> [*]
    RolledBack --> [*]
```
workflow: propose with rationale → impact analysis → approve by authority → activate with prior version preserved → publish → monitor emergence
EVO.privacy: Evolution of privacy-relevant subjects triggers consent re-evaluation; changes cannot silently widen data use.
EVO.audit: Every change records rationale, authority, impact, and prior state. History is never rewritten — only superseded.
EVO.twin: Evolution drives twin model versioning; a twin's history is as valuable as its current state.
EVO.agent: Evolution Agent proposes changes from observed drift; Emergence Agent detects system-level properties for governance review.
EVO.runtime: Version resolution prefers latest activated; historical queries time-travel via the version chain.
EVO.scaling: Version chains are append-only and shard by subject; time-travel queries are bounded by retention policy.
EVO.multiTenant: Tenant-level evolution cannot alter shared ontology; shared changes go through the Evolution Authority.
EVO.geo: Evolution activation is jurisdiction-aware; a change legal in one region rolls out per regional policy.
EVO.failure: Breaking change without deprecation, orphaned version chain, emergence runaway, rollback failure.
EVO.recovery: Rollback is a first-class command that activates the prior version — never a data restore. History remains intact either way.
EVO.certification: Evolution must pass impact analysis, deprecation path (for breaking changes), authority jurisdiction, and history preservation.
EVO.migration: Migration IS evolution — there is no separate migration path. All changes flow through this domain.
EVO.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Proposer
    participant EV as Evolution Domain
    participant AU as Authority
    P->>EV: propose(change, rationale)
    EV->>EV: impact analysis
```
